# Render vs Heroku in 2026: Pricing, Features & Which to Choose

**Short answer: Render is generally the better choice for new projects in 2026, particularly if you want modern deployment features, managed databases, and predictable pricing. Heroku remains attractive if you value its mature ecosystem, established workflows, and extensive add-on marketplace.**

Both platforms support deploying web applications, APIs, background workers, and databases without managing your own servers.

Here's how they compare as of November 2026.

## 1. Pricing comparison

### Render pricing

[Render official pricing](https://render.com/pricing?trk=public_profile__reactions-text&utm_source=chatgpt.com)

Render uses a combination of workspace subscriptions and usage-based compute pricing.

| Resource | Monthly price |
|---|---:|
| Static sites | Free |
| Free web service | $0 |
| Starter web service (512 MB) | $7 |
| Standard web service (2 GB) | $25 |
| Larger web services | $85+ |
| PostgreSQL (256 MB) | $6 |
| PostgreSQL (1 GB) | $19 |
| Redis-compatible storage | $10+ |
| Hobby workspace | Free |
| Pro workspace | $25 |

Additional costs can include storage, bandwidth, and build minutes.

### Heroku pricing

[Heroku official pricing](https://www.heroku.com/pricing/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

Heroku uses dynos (application containers) and separately priced data services.

| Resource | Monthly price |
|---|---:|
| Eco dyno (512 MB) | $5 |
| Basic dyno (512 MB) | $7 |
| Standard-1X (512 MB) | $25 |
| Standard-2X (1 GB) | $50 |
| Performance-M (2.5 GB) | $250 |
| Performance-L (14 GB) | $500 |
| PostgreSQL Essential-0 | $5 |
| PostgreSQL Essential-1 | $9 |
| PostgreSQL Essential-2 | $20 |
| Key-Value Store Mini | $3 |

Heroku also offers higher-performance, private-networking, and compliance-focused infrastructure.

### Which is cheaper?

For a small production application:

| Component | Render | Heroku |
|---|---:|---:|
| Web application | $7 | $7 |
| PostgreSQL | $6 | $5 |
| **Total** | **$13/month** | **$12/month** |

These are illustrative starting configurations, excluding additional usage charges.

Heroku is marginally cheaper in this particular example, but Render offers more flexibility in choosing compute resources.

## 2. Feature comparison

| Feature | Render | Heroku |
|---|---|---|
| GitHub integration | Yes | Yes |
| Automatic deployments | Yes | Yes |
| Docker support | Yes | Yes |
| Node.js | Yes | Yes |
| Python | Yes | Yes |
| Ruby | Yes | Yes |
| Go | Yes | Yes |
| Java | Yes | Yes |
| PostgreSQL | Managed | Managed |
| Redis-compatible storage | Yes | Yes |
| Background workers | Yes | Yes |
| Cron jobs | Yes | Via add-ons or scheduling |
| Static websites | Free | Requires alternative hosting |
| Private networking | Yes | Yes |
| Autoscaling | Yes, paid plans | Yes, eligible plans |
| Preview environments | Yes | Via pipelines/review apps |
| Custom domains | Yes | Yes |
| Automatic SSL | Yes | Yes |
| SSH access | Yes | Platform-specific access |
| Infrastructure as code | Yes | Yes |

### Where Render stands out

**1. Modern deployment experience**

- Connect a GitHub repository.
- Automatically build and deploy on every push.
- Supports Docker and native runtimes.
- Supports automatic deployments and rollbacks.
- Offers preview environments.

**2. Built-in infrastructure**

Render provides:
- Web services.
- Background workers.
- PostgreSQL databases.
- Redis-compatible key-value storage.
- Cron jobs.
- Static websites.
- Private services.

You can run most of your application infrastructure within one platform.

**3. Flexible compute pricing**

Render offers multiple CPU and RAM configurations, scaling up to 12 CPUs and 96 GB RAM for its listed web-service configurations.

**4. Static website hosting**

Render provides free static website hosting with:
- Global CDN.
- Automatic deployments.
- Custom domains.
- Managed TLS certificates.

This is particularly convenient for React, Vue, Angular, and Next.js static deployments.

### Where Heroku stands out

**1. Mature developer ecosystem**

Heroku has been around for a long time and has a mature ecosystem of integrations, add-ons, and deployment workflows.

**2. Dyno management**

Heroku handles application containers through dynos.

You get:
- Process management.
- Application logging.
- Horizontal scaling.
- Background workers.
- Deployment management.
- Application metrics.

**3. Extensive data services**

Heroku offers:
- Heroku Postgres.
- Heroku Key-Value Store.
- Apache Kafka.
- Advanced database configurations.

**4. Enterprise capabilities**

Heroku has dedicated infrastructure options:

- Private Spaces.
- Shield plans.
- HIPAA-oriented compliance options.
- Private networking.
- Enterprise security capabilities.

This makes Heroku particularly relevant for organizations with established enterprise requirements.

---

## 3. Free tier comparison

This is an important distinction.

| Feature | Render | Heroku |
|---|---|---|
| Free web hosting | Yes | No |
| Free static hosting | Yes | No equivalent native static hosting |
| Free PostgreSQL | Yes, with limitations | No |
| Free Redis | Limited | No |
| Free always-on application | No | No |
| Free production-ready database | No | No |

**Render's free tier:**
- Free web services.
- Free static sites.
- Limited free PostgreSQL.
- Free services have resource and availability limitations.

**Heroku's cheapest option:**
- Eco dyno: $5/month.
- Sleeps after 30 minutes of inactivity.
- Basic dyno: $7/month and stays running.

For experimentation, prototypes, and hobby projects, Render has a clear advantage.

---

## 4. Developer experience and deployment

Both platforms are relatively easy to use, but their approaches differ.

| Category | Render | Heroku |
|---|---|---|
| Initial setup | Very easy | Very easy |
| Git-based deployment | Excellent | Excellent |
| Docker deployment | Excellent | Excellent |
| Configuration | YAML / Dashboard | Procfile / Dashboard |
| Buildpacks | Yes, native runtimes | Yes |
| Logs | Built-in | Built-in |
| Environment variables | Yes | Yes |
| Rollbacks | Yes | Yes |
| CI/CD integration | Good | Excellent ecosystem |
| Documentation | Good | Extensive |

My take:

- **Render:** Better experience for developers starting new projects.
- **Heroku:** Particularly convenient for teams already invested in its ecosystem.

## 5. Pros and cons

### Render

**Pros**
- Generous free offering.
- Competitive compute pricing.
- Free static website hosting.
- Managed PostgreSQL.
- Docker support.
- Automatic deployments.
- Background workers and cron jobs.
- Modern infrastructure.
- Good fit for full-stack applications.

**Cons**
- Free web services can spin down after inactivity.
- Free databases have limitations.
- Some advanced enterprise capabilities require expensive plans.
- Smaller add-on ecosystem than Heroku.

### Heroku

**Pros**
- Mature and reliable platform.
- Excellent developer experience.
- Extensive add-on ecosystem.
- Strong PostgreSQL offering.
- Excellent application management.
- Enterprise networking and security features.
- Well-established documentation.

**Cons**
- No free application hosting.
- Performance can become expensive.
- Eco dynos sleep.
- Additional services can increase overall costs.
- Less attractive pricing for some small applications.

---

## 6. Which should you choose in 2026?

| Use case | My recommendation |
|---|---|
| Personal projects | Render |
| MVP development | Render |
| SaaS applications | Render |
| React / Next.js applications | Render |
| Node.js APIs | Render |
| Python / Django applications | Render |
| PostgreSQL-backed applications | Either |
| Background workers | Either |
| Enterprise applications | Heroku or Render Scale |
| Existing Heroku infrastructure | Heroku |
| Cost-conscious startups | Render |

## 7. My final verdict

I'd give Render the advantage for most new application deployments in 2026.

| Category | Winner |
|---|---|
| Pricing | Render |
| Free tier | Render |
| Developer experience | Render |
| Static hosting | Render |
| PostgreSQL | Tie |
| Enterprise capabilities | Heroku |
| Add-on ecosystem | Heroku |
| Modern application deployment | Render |
| Small SaaS hosting | Render |

### My recommendation

**Choose Render if:**
- You're building a new SaaS product.
- You want affordable hosting.
- You use Node.js, Python, Django, FastAPI, or Next.js.
- You want PostgreSQL and background workers.
- You want to minimize infrastructure management.

**Choose Heroku if:**
- You're maintaining an existing Heroku application.
- You depend on specific Heroku add-ons.
- You need its established enterprise infrastructure.
- Your team already has extensive Heroku experience.

### Official pricing pages

- [Render Pricing](https://render.com/pricing?utm_source=chatgpt.com)
- [Heroku Pricing](https://www.heroku.com/pricing/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

**Bottom line:** For a new startup or SaaS application, I'd start with Render. Heroku is still a capable platform, but Render offers a compelling combination of pricing, infrastructure, and developer experience.
